Nav-bar avatar

.dr-avatar-sm · .dr-op__name · components/avatar.css · components/card.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Ivan K.
  1. 1.dr-avatar-smThe disc: 28px, --bg-well ground, radius 999, overflow: hidden.
  2. 2.dr-avatar-sm imgThe operator's photograph, object-fit: cover, alt="" because the name beside it says who it is.
  3. 3.dr-op__nameThe operator's name, 8 after the disc (the bar's gap), at the heading step, 15/600, in --text-primary.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Nav-bar avatar.

States

No state of its own: the disc and the name are a label, not a control. The bar's notification bell carries its own states; the availability badge is not a control.

When to use

The nav-bar avatar puts the operator's own face at the leading edge of his home bar, where the client's bar carries the DRON mark. It stands on operator-listings and operator-listings-empty only.

28 is derived, not picked: the nav bar is 56, so the disc is exactly half the bar and centres with 14 above and below (measured 13.6 / 14.4, the 0.8 being the bar's hairline). None of the other avatar rungs fits a bar: 117 is the operator panel's width, 120 is a subject, 176 is a call screen's middle, and 20 is a badge on an avatar. The disc's --bg-well ground closed the last place a painted page read a colour from the grayscale sheet.

The name is the operator's own short form: first name and initial, Ivan K.

Sources: DESIGN.md § The nav-bar avatar · ui/kit.html § Nav bar · operator home · inventory.md § 1 (Nav-bar avatar)

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Ivan K.

On the operator's home: who is signed in, at the leading edge, half the bar's height.

Don’t

Ivan K.

A larger avatar rung forced into the 56px bar. The 56 disc fills the bar edge to edge and leaves the face no air. Keep .dr-avatar-sm in the bar; a face that is the subject of the screen belongs in a profile head. A pushed screen leads with the back chevron, never with a face.
